name: Neutral
_comment: DEFAULT brand profile. Used whenever a project does not supply its own branding.
A neutral slate-and-grey palette, the system font pair, and NO wordmark, so a document never
carries any firm's identity by accident. For a client's own look, copy _example-customer.json.
Contrast (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for body text): band_text on band 14.5:1, header_text on
header_fill 14.3:1, body_text on white 14.7:1.

fonts._comment: Both pairs are the system pair: they ship on every machine, so a client who opens and edits the file sees what we saw. A client profile may set a different 'brand' pair.

_type_scale_comment: THREE heading levels, distinguished by SIZE, not by inventing more colours:
subsection 11pt  on the HEADER fill     (medium) - shares the column-header fill on purpose,
so a sub-section reads as attached to the columns
beneath it instead of floating in the table
An earlier version gave sub-sections band-colour text with no fill and only a bottom rule. On a
tab with several stacked tables per section (WD Solution - O4I) that made 'CSV Format' look
like it was floating loose in the table above it rather than labelling the columns below.
_logo_comment: No wordmark. The styler then leaves any picture already in the workbook exactly as it is (no resize, no re-anchor) and styles each tab title in place. A client profile sets asset, ratio and width_pt.

conventions._comment: open_item_fill is a WORKING convention, not branding: yellow means 'missing info / needs follow-up'. Never restyle it, whatever the brand. Same for semantic status colours driven by conditional formatting (RAG scales, test-status rules) - those carry meaning.

_comment: One body height per TABLE (the worst row in that table), then structural rows as RATIOS of
it: band 1.3, header 1.0, sub-section 0.7. Ratios so they self-scale with the type scale.
SOURCE: hand-measured off the author's cleaned copy of the reference IDD, where a File table
body of 41.2pt sat under a 54.0 band (1.31), a 41.2 header (1.00) and a 28.5 sub-section
(0.69). NOT taken from xlsx_calibrate.py: its rhythm pass reported band 0.55 / header 0.58 /
subsection null, which is wrong — it associates a band with a table by 'nearest band above',
and body heights across the book range 15-55pt so the mode is not a stable base. Fix that
measurement before trusting calibrated rhythm values.
Uniform-to-worst is only safe AFTER col_roles has fixed the widths — otherwise one starved
prose column forces every row in the table to its height.
Width weight by column ROLE, relative to a label column. CALIBRATED by xlsx_calibrate.py
from the author's cleaned copy: prose median 75.0pt, label 22.0, name 22.7, flag 12.1.
Role comes from the header text (Notes/Description/Purpose/Logic -> prose; Required/Status/
Enabled/Date -> flag; Name/Field/Type/Value -> name; else label). Measured content length is
a tiebreaker WITHIN a role, not the whole allocation — minimising the worst column forced
short-label columns toward parity with prose columns, which is why Requirements' empty
'Notes' column collapsed to 9.1 when the author had set it to 50.6.
No per-tab panel treatments. 'panel' (one header-fill block behind a prose-only tab's content)
was evaluated for READ ME and DECLINED 2026-08-10: the contrast gate already yields a clean,
readable READ ME on white that matches the author's hand-cleaned geometry within rounding, and a
fill behind body prose re-introduces the contrast risk the gate exists to remove. Keep prose-only
tabs on white. Re-add a slug->'panel' entry here only if a future brand explicitly wants it.
